LOL I'm a scientist, so I actually read the paper - even though it's outside of my domain. Well, I read the important bits. This isn't technically my domain, but I've acquired the skill of reading scientific publications. It's a handy skill to develop, 'cause science journalism is shit.

1. Read the abstract.
  2. Read the first three paragraphs of the content.
  3. Skim through and look for tables, graphs, and images.
  4. Check names of citations.
  5. Scroll back up and read conclusions - to see if they gibe with the rest.
  6. Go back through, if necessary, to see if the data agrees.
  7. Make sure you understand what the paper claims to be answering (this can be deceptive).
  8. Run a quick sanity check (if needed) for p-hacking and math conclusions (where applicable).
  9. Check abstract a final time to see if they actually answer the questions they said they did. (See #7.)

There... That's how you read a scientific publication quickly. If it's really interesting, settle down and read it all - but I only do so when I'm really interested in the topic.
